question: How much cash did Apple generate in FY2023, and how did it return it to shareholders?

answer.summary: Apple generated $110.54B of operating cash flow in FY2023 [F00224] and spent $10.96B on property, plant and equipment [F00236], producing $99.58B of free cash flow [F01389]. It returned $92.58B to shareholders [F01448], comprising $77.55B of share repurchases [F00251] and $15.03B of dividends [F00248], equal to 93.0% of free cash flow [F01451]. Cash, cash equivalents and unrestricted marketable securities totaled $148.3B as of September 30, 2023 [T00350]. Total net sales decreased 3%, or $11.0 billion, in FY2023 versus FY2022 [T00275].

drivers: Share repurchases of $77.55B [F00251] were the larger component of the $92.58B total shareholder return [F01448], with dividends of $15.03B [F00248] the smaller component; the two sum to the reported total.
The $92.58B returned [F01448] absorbed 93.0% of the $99.58B free cash flow [F01389] [F01451], so nearly all FY2023 free cash flow was paid out.
Operating cash flow of $110.54B [F00224] less capex of $10.96B [F00236] reconciles to the $99.58B free cash flow [F01389].
risks_and_red_flags: Total net sales fell 3% ($11.0B) in FY2023 versus FY2022, with FX weakness accounting for more than the entire decrease and lower Mac and iPhone sales only partially offset by Services [T00275].
A 93.0% payout of free cash flow [F01451] leaves a thin FCF cushion if operating cash flow weakens.

The company uses commercial paper proceeds for general corporate purposes including dividends and share repurchases; $6.0B was outstanding at September 30, 2023 at a 5.28% weighted-average rate, up from $10.0B at 2.31% a year earlier [T00548].
